pain: Independent worker invoices rejected or unpaid for weeks
quote_or_finding: My poor support worker has not been paid for 2 months. I have lost 2 carers due to late/non payment of invoices.

pain: Late payment by self-managed provider
quote_or_finding: This provider says it will pay invoices in 7 to 10 days but I have been waiting a month

pain: Getting invoices paid
quote_or_finding: absolute nightmare

pain: Invoices fail format rules
quote_or_finding: Provider reply: invoices unpaid because supplier was "submitting invoices that didn't match our system requirements"

pain: Service names must match official list
quote_or_finding: If you use different names, your invoice might be delayed or sent back to you.

pain: Stacked fees and delays paying workers via Mable
quote_or_finding: Then told it's a two week delay for our workers getting paid. Mable is horrible to deal with and then we get hit with fees from Mable and then a fee from homemade to process Mable's invoice.

pain: Workers unpaid over a month after rollout
quote_or_finding: Some support workers went without pay for more than a month against a usual window of about a week

pain: AT-HM quoting workload with little funding flowing
quote_or_finding: Suppliers are "doing more work than ever" providing quotes and information; process is "quite a problematic one" (Serena Ovens, ATSA CEO)

pain: AT-HM inconsistent and unclear
quote_or_finding: OTA adviser Christina Wyatt: rollout shows a concerning lack of consistency and clarity for all affected parties

pain: Equipment invoice unpaid for months
quote_or_finding: My dad needs this rollator for his neuropathy and I have been given one excuse after another.

pain: AT-HM claims lack evidence
quote_or_finding: Only 23% of AT-HM claims had sufficient evidence of agreed price; 50% had sufficient evidence of delivery
source: Dept of Health payment integrity Cycle 1 report

pain: Cannot prove the price was agreed
quote_or_finding: just 35 per cent of all claims had sufficient evidence of agreed price

pain: Evidence gaps across claims
quote_or_finding: Cycle 1 "identified significant gaps in the documentary evidence submitted by the providers"
source: Dept of Health Cycle 1 summary report

pain: Statements non-compliant
quote_or_finding: 21% of 262 monthly statements reviewed had all required inclusions
quote_type: official finding (one search excerpt; a second search could not confirm the 21% figure)
status: dropped: Governa AI and platforms cover statements

pain: Admin load per hour of care
quote_or_finding: About 31 minutes of admin and compliance per hour of direct care (Advance Ageing WA to Senate inquiry)
status: dropped: too broad for a 2-week MVP

pain: Care management time must be logged in 15-minute blocks per client and claimed in arrears
quote_or_finding: Spreadsheets become unworkable at scale (VIPS Care article)
status: killed: Visualcare / Lookout / Statura / CareVision / Five Good Friends all ship it

pain: Statements confusing; double billing visible
quote_or_finding: Pearl Home Care: $4.4M error affecting 1872 clients left double charges on statements
status: killed: Wayly already sells a statement decoder

pain: Charged HELF for services they cannot use
quote_or_finding: Higher Everyday Living Fees are optional. (Commissioner Liz Hefren-Webb); 199 fee complaints in first half of 2026
status: killed: Centrim Life / helf.services / Pluss / e-Tools / Inerva cover provider side

pain: Care minutes audit: reconciling evidence across systems
quote_or_finding: Providers flag time burden of pulling evidence and reconciling systems for the audited Care Minutes Performance Statement (due 31 Oct 2026)

pain: AI rostering makes hours less predictable
quote_or_finding: UWU survey: 19% saw changes to shifts or hours, 20% less predictable hours, 15% less work

pain: Favouritism in shift allocation
quote_or_finding: Workers allege managers give the best shifts to friends (Aged Care Worker Support Group on Facebook)

pain: CHSP providers not ready for Support at Home
quote_or_finding: 85% of CHSP-only providers not confident (Ageing Australia survey)
status: killed: government abandoned the merger in Aug 2026

pain: Mable pay speed and fee transparency
quote_or_finding: the way it handles fees and pay is disappointing and not transparent

pain: Cannot find a residential respite bed
quote_or_finding: Six in 10 carers reported difficulty finding high-quality respite; nearly 60 per cent reported difficulty finding available services in their local area (2025 Carer Wellbeing Survey)
source: Dementia Australia and Carers Australia joint position statement

pain: Respite close to impossible; told to call back later
quote_or_finding: Care concierge Kate Montgomerie says respite has become close to impossible to get; providers say waitlists for permanent beds mean they cannot hold beds for respite

pain: Minimum stays and no local supply
quote_or_finding: Many providers of residential respite care require minimum four-week stays; Carers ACT reported almost no residential respite available

pain: Waiting years for a permanent bed
quote_or_finding: Betty Cameron has waited two years for a residential bed for her husband with dementia in South Australia; federal report puts the average wait at 365 days

pain: No live availability anywhere
quote_or_finding: your approval for respite care does not guarantee a place

pain: Stuck in hospital waiting for a bed
quote_or_finding: More than 3,600 people in hospital waiting for an aged care place in mid 2026, up from over 2,700 in mid 2025
status: context for idea 4; hospitals are an enterprise sale

pain: Charged HELF for meals and services that should be included
quote_or_finding: We are very concerned about the use of Higher Everyday Living Fees in relation to meals. This is not optional. This is not an additional service.

pain: Paying for services the resident cannot use
quote_or_finding: Family billed $52 a day for Foxtel, outings, newspapers and wine, including services a resident with dementia could not use

pain: Fee changes cause panic
quote_or_finding: 'I won't be eating' (headline quote); a resident's husband fears costs rising by about $14,000 a year

pain: Refunds happen only after regulator action
quote_or_finding: Opal HealthCare refunded or credited almost $200,000 to almost 350 residents after a Commission review

pain: Each home has its own application form
quote_or_finding: Most families apply to between three and six homes; most facilities have their own application form separate from My Aged Care
status: below bar: no one found complaining about the forms

pain: No GP will visit
quote_or_finding: AMA position statement: residents cannot get regular GP care; regional homes turning residents away

pain: Not enough time; reforms added paperwork
quote_or_finding: 49.03% of 3552 respondents reported insufficient time to provide care; respondents said reforms increased the admin burden on RNs

pain: Complaints rising; families are the main complainants
quote_or_finding: 10,628 complaints 1 Nov 2025 to 30 Jun 2026 versus 7,323 a year earlier; top concerns staffing, care planning and fees
source: ACQSC Annual Report 2025-26 via The Ageing Agenda
